newsitem.title: LEBANON: Lebanon, Kuwait, Egypt brokers sign trading deals.
newsitem.headline: Lebanon, Kuwait, Egypt brokers sign trading deals.

text.p: Brokers from the Lebanese, Egyptian and Kuwait stock exchanges signed agreements on Friday to start cross-trading equities early in January.

"A total of 121 bilateral cooperation agreements were signed between brokerage houses working in the three stock exchanges," Sa'faq al-Rukeibi, secretary-general of the Union of Arab Stock Exchanges, told Reuters at the end of a meeting of some 80 brokers.
The brokers' agreements effectively bypass the unresolved issue of cross-listing of shares on the three bourses.
Earlier this year the exchanges reached framework accords on cross-trading, clearance and settlement, but cross-listing has been delayed by the lack of common listing criteria.
Ziad Makkawi of Beirut-based Middle East Capital Group said the deals "basically allow me to offer Egyptian and Kuwait equity to my investor base and for them to do the same."

Brokers said the Lebanese and Egyptian exchanges were open to investors from all three countries, In Kuwait investors from Egypt and Lebanon can buy only investment and real-estate funds for the time being.
Rukeibi said Kuwaiti authorities were working on opening up their stock exchange to non-Kuwaiti investors for direct share ownership but the process needed time.
Cross-trading would begin either on January 7 or 8, he said.

"Cross-listing of shares will no longer be an obstacle after the signing of the agreement. Why? Because any broker in his home country, say a Kuwaiti, can fully invest in the Lebanese market or the Egyptian markets," Rukeibi added.

In September, the three exchanges signed a deal in Beirut to begin cross-trading of shares next year. In its first stage, the deal guarantees a free flow of updated information to investors and dealers in the three markets.

In October, a cooperation agreement was signed in Cairo between the companies which handle clearing and settlement for the three exchanges -- Misr Clearing Co of Egypt, Midclear of Lebanon and the Kuwaiti Clearing Co.
Stock exchange officials and brokers at the Beirut meeting said cross-listing was still down the road, mainly because of the lack of common listing criteria.
"To have cross-listing in all the companies, you need to have the same criteria. It needs time," Gabriel Sehnaoui, Chairman of the Beirut Stock Exchange, told Reuters.
Makawi said: "The idea is to move to an integrated regional equity market...but I think cross-listing is still a little bit down the road, though these things tend to move in leaps."

The market capitalisation of the Egyptian exchange is $10.5 billion and the Kuwait bourse's is $18 billion. The Beirut Stock Exchange, which re-opened in January after a shutdown of nearly 13 years, has a total capitalisation of about $2.4 billion.
